title: Hypertension Management: Contemporary Guideline Updates and Therapeutic Sequencing
summary: Current guidance emphasizes accurate diagnosis with out-of-office monitoring, earlier combination therapy, and aggressive cardiovascular risk reduction. First-line agents remain thiazide-like diuretics, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, and calcium-channel blockers, with beta-blockers reserved for specific indications. Target <130/80 mmHg for most high-risk adults; use single-pill combinations to improve adherence. SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs reduce CV events in diabetes and CKD and are complementary to BP therapy.
clinicalQuestion: How should clinicians diagnose hypertension accurately, individualize BP targets, and sequence antihypertensive therapies in 2025 to reduce cardiovascular, renal, and mortality outcomes?

heroStats.label: Target BP in most high-risk adults

keyMoments.title: Earlier combination therapy
keyMoments.body: Initiate two agents (ideally single-pill) for stage 2 HTN or ≥20/10 mmHg above goal; improves speed to control and adherence.

keyMoments.title: Out-of-office confirmation
keyMoments.body: Use HBPM or ABPM to confirm diagnosis and exclude white coat/masked hypertension before labeling and lifelong therapy.

keyMoments.title: Intensive targets in high-risk
keyMoments.body: Target <130 mmHg systolic in most high-risk adults without orthostatic intolerance; balance benefits vs. adverse events.

keyMoments.title: Resistant hypertension pathway
keyMoments.body: Optimize triple therapy, add mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, screen for secondary causes (esp. primary aldosteronism, OSA).

sections.title: Confirming Hypertension and Setting Evidence-Based Targets
sections.blurb: Prioritize accurate measurement, risk stratification, and individualized goals.

steps.title: Confirm with ABPM/HBPM before diagnosis
steps.body: Use standardized office BP and confirm with ABPM/HBPM to detect white coat and masked hypertension. **SPRINT** showed **SBP target <120 mmHg reduced MACE (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.64–0.89)** but increased some adverse events, supporting lower targets in high-risk adults [1].

steps.title: Set targets by risk
steps.body: Aim **<130/80 mmHg** for most adults with established ASCVD, CKD, diabetes, or high 10-year risk per contemporary guidelines [2], [3]. Older, frail adults may require individualized goals to avoid orthostatic hypotension; monitor standing BP and symptoms.

steps.title: Lifestyle as foundation
steps.body: Implement sodium reduction, weight loss, DASH-style diet, physical activity, alcohol moderation, and sleep optimization. Lifestyle often lowers SBP by **5–20 mmHg cumulatively** and augments pharmacotherapy.

sections.title: First-Line Choices and Combination Strategies
sections.blurb: Use long-acting, outcome-proven agents and simplify regimens.

steps.title: Choose initial therapy
steps.body: First-line classes: **thiazide-like diuretics (chlorthalidone/indapamide), ACE inhibitors or ARBs, and dihydropyridine CCBs**. Thiazide-like diuretics have superior outcome data vs. HCTZ; consider chlorthalidone for high CV risk or resistant cases [2], [3].

steps.title: Start combination for stage 2 HTN
steps.body: If baseline BP is **≥20/10 mmHg above goal (≈≥150/90 mmHg)**, initiate **two complementary agents** (ACEi/ARB + CCB or ACEi/ARB + thiazide-like diuretic), preferably as a **single-pill combination** to improve adherence and BP control [2], [3].

steps.title: Compelling indications drive class choice
steps.body: CKD with albuminuria: **ACEi/ARB**; HFrEF: **ACEi/ARB/ARNI + beta-blocker + MRA + SGLT2 inhibitor**; Post-MI or angina: **beta-blocker + ACEi/ARB**; Atrial fibrillation rate control: **beta-blocker**; Pregnancy: **labetalol, nifedipine ER, methyldopa**.

sections.title: CKD, Diabetes, and Older Adults
sections.blurb: Integrate BP targets with cardiorenal protection.

steps.title: Chronic kidney disease
steps.body: Use **ACEi/ARB** for albuminuric CKD. Add **SGLT2 inhibitor** (e.g., dapagliflozin, empagliflozin) for eGFR thresholds per labels; **DAPA-CKD** showed **RR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51–0.72)** for the renal composite, with modest BP lowering, complementing RAAS blockade [4]. Consider **finerenone** in diabetic CKD with albuminuria (FIDELIO/FIGARO).

steps.title: Type 2 diabetes
steps.body: Target **<130/80 mmHg** with RAAS blockade for albuminuria. Add **SGLT2 inhibitors** or **GLP-1 receptor agonists** for ASCVD/CKD benefits independent of BP. **EMPA-REG OUTCOME** reduced CV death (**HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49–0.77**) [5].

steps.title: Older adults and frailty
steps.body: Intensive control reduces CV events, but monitor for **orthostatic hypotension, AKI, and electrolyte disturbances**. De-intensify if symptomatic or with falls; prioritize long-acting, low-dose combinations.

sections.title: Stepwise Approach to Resistant Hypertension
sections.blurb: Confirm true resistance and add targeted therapies.

steps.title: Verify and address adherence and measurement
steps.body: Confirm with ABPM/HBPM, assess adherence, and eliminate agents raising BP (NSAIDs, decongestants). Ensure optimized triple therapy at maximally tolerated doses: **ACEi/ARB + long-acting dihydropyridine CCB + thiazide-like diuretic**.

steps.title: Add mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
steps.body: If still above goal, add **spironolactone**; **PATHWAY-2** demonstrated **greater SBP reduction vs. bisoprolol or doxazosin** in resistant HTN, supporting aldosterone excess as a driver [6]. Monitor **K+ and eGFR**.

steps.title: Screen for secondary causes
steps.body: Evaluate for **primary aldosteronism, renal artery stenosis, CKD progression, OSA, pheochromocytoma, Cushing’s, and thyroid disease**. Treat reversible causes and consider referral for renal denervation in selected patients after failure of optimized pharmacotherapy.

sections.title: Practical Tips, Safety, and Follow-Up
sections.blurb: Monitor closely after medication changes; use single-pill combinations whenever possible.

cards.title: Baseline and Monitoring
items: Check BMP, electrolytes, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio; repeat 1–2 weeks after RAAS or diuretic changes.
Assess orthostatic vitals in older adults or with symptoms.
Use HBPM protocol: 2 readings, twice daily, 7 days; discard day 1, average remaining.

cards.title: Safety Watchouts
items: ACEi/ARB: hyperkalemia, creatinine rise (acceptable up to 30%).
CCBs: edema; consider RAAS blocker combination to mitigate.
Spironolactone: hyperkalemia, gynecomastia; consider eplerenone if intolerant.

cards.title: When to Escalate/Refer
items: Resistant HTN after optimized triple therapy and MRA.
Suspected secondary hypertension or abrupt onset/worsening.
Intolerance to multiple first-line classes or recurrent hypertensive emergencies.

cards.title: Therapy Optimization
items: Prefer chlorthalidone/indapamide over HCTZ for potency and outcomes.
Use single-pill combinations to enhance adherence and faster control.
Align antihypertensives with comorbid indications (HFrEF, CKD, CAD, AF).
